Ngh!
I'll strip you bare!

...tell me who the British Intelligence agent is.

...every first-rate spy is a coward...defection...just thinking of it terrifies me...

You answer first. Are you the watcher or the Fog?

Stubborn fool. You just will not let go...
A first-rate spy...you must be important...
Talk! I'll strangle you!

I am the one asking questions.
You bastard...
Should I give him time...?
Go wash your face and try again.
That is my line!
No. This ship is not a playground for intelligence agents.
Tell me! Who is with British Intelligence?
We are at an impasse...
There is one Russian spy here...
I will keep you secret from the English dogs. Think it over. While you people wage your petty quarrel between nations, this ship is sinking.

...the "Russian Fog."

No.

A long shot...
Stravinsky!

Stra

You fool!
Listen...
What?! Are you threatening me? I reject violence! It is the enemy of world peace!

A genius chooses his surroundings.
I'd like to choose too.
You said yourself that you are fleeing Russia.
...the Russian secret police are aboard this ship? No! I will not go back to that country! Help me! I want asylum in America! Take me to the captain!

He needs freedom!
Who do you think you are?!
A creator. Any complaints?
If you survive until tomorrow, I'll take you to the captain.
Really?
Whatever.
Wait...america? Not Britain?

I hate people who live on instinct alone...
...I understand. Thank you...

It's true. I
watched them. Not one of them left their seat.
...you watched them.
An alibi...
Why are you here?
Why indeed?
...you're a good person, Ilyu. That short hair suits you.
You don't look at me like I'm a tramp.
A perfect alibi...too perfect.

Truth and reality are different. Reality can mean anything, depending on how you look at it.

In an ordinary detective novel, perhaps...
Wait...
This child...
That much...
Who taught you fortune-telling?

From my grandmother...she always gazed at the foothills of Kuru Fostel in the evening mist. My silent grandmother...a poison laced with happiness took her voice. Before she lost the power of speech, she often told my fortune...
How sad...
Do you like fortune-telling?
...far away, beyond the drifting mist...something sometimes glints. What is it? Can you not sense it?
It says this girl is innocent...
But I'm not much good at deciding things like that...
You are ready to narrow down the culprit, aren't you?
Correct.
Search to the west.
There is a mountain.
A woodcutter lives there.
Ask the woodcutter the way, and you will find a path leading north...
...all right. Thank you...
First-Class Cabin C
Lumeranka
This stays between us. This secret is yours and mine alone. Tell no one. Understand? Not a soul!
About Princess Tianon?
Indeed.
Please, tell me.
Swear you will tell no one!
All right.
The truth is, Princess Tianon is the third daughter of the Maharaja of Renan, in India. His name is Kasamara Hatoz Tos Harandoil Kurumayubi Agero Kyuryo Kokoron Urero Yunna Uappa...
Dawn will break first.
Keep the name short, please.
That was the short version!
How do you remember it all?
I have recited it since the last Maharaja's day!
Enough. I understand. She is traveling incognito, then?
This whole affair is the work of the chancellor, who schemes to seize the throne...
The chancellor?!

I believe he arranged it to kill the princess. The Maharaja had nineteen children. All but Tianon were poisoned. She lives in fear of sharing their fate and has closed her heart to the world. This journey abroad was meant to bring her peace...poor child...
Boo-hoo-hoo-hoo...
I cannot listen to any more of this.
Well, I should be going...
Wait!
Yes?
Stay and cry with me! Boo-hoo-hoo...
Tianon and Lumeranka are cleared.
That much is certain, but...
A maharaja's daughter from a British Indian protectorate, and her chaperone. Time to narrow the targets: Ashby or Ruthie.
And you.
I'm sick of this.
Still complaining?
Question Ruthie. She was the first to discover Braque's murder. Braque was obsessed with the "Russian Fog." If she killed him, she may well be a Russian spy.
Adjoining Room C
Ruthie
...you suspect me, don't you? Because Braque died that way...
...may I be a little cruel?
Go ahead...hee hee. You're a strange detective.
I hate what this job is turning me into...
...it isn't you I doubt. I doubt my own first impression of you...
So your first impression of me wasn't entirely bad? I'm flattered.
Anyone would feel that way...
When did you meet Braque?
Two years ago. I was a sales clerk at a trading company. I was good with figures, so Braque noticed me and recruited me.
I was so happy. I grew up in a small town in southern France and dreamed of Paris: the Metro, boulevard cafes, and becoming a woman whose talent no one could match.
That faraway look...
I thought women were finally being recognized. But Braque only wanted a pretty woman he could take anywhere.
...that's why you can kill him.
Is that what you think?
Too soft, Kasuke. You're letting her charm win you over...
Women are demons, remember? You're a full-fledged detective now! Do it!
Here is my theory. You and Braque conspired to hijack the ship. Partway through, you tired of working with him, killed your partner, and meant to finish the plan alone.
Reality is ambiguous. People interpret it only as they wish to see it. Is that how it appears to you?
...that theory is a stretch...
Your motive is weak, but you hated Braque.
With enough passion to kill him?
...no. She's as conflicted as any city dweller...
Come on! Spit it out! Talk, damn you! Say anything!
...that doesn't suit you. Aren't you trying too hard?
I'm just desperate!
You like your work, don't you?
I suppose I do...
You only like yourself when you're working.
I hate work. Does anyone really like it?
Some do.
You think you're a career woman second to none?
Professional narcissism
cannot truly save a person's life.
Do you believe your abilities will always sustain you?
I can't afford doubts now.
Do you enjoy Paris?
...if I'm not alone...
That hits home...
You couldn't do it. Your world exists inside fashion magazines.
Maybe...yes, perhaps it does.
You're drunk on life in Paris.
...perhaps I am.
You're detached.
I feel as though I've seen something terribly cold.
I can't truly hate anyone. I don't know what I should do or what I ever really wanted. When you never find it, you become vague. I found nothing in the city...
Nostalgia...it's a lovely name for a ship.
I'm too soft...someday a woman will deceive me...
Mediterranean colors...words that make me hate Paris.
She's innocent. She couldn't have done it...trust your instincts more.
...who suggested the tea party?
Lord Ashby.
All right!
